summary.intent: Drive the caliper PropType-variants work (stacked PRs #388-#391) to merge: address review findings on slice 1 (#391), resolve merge conflicts with main, and keep the remaining slices moving.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 PRs #386, #387, #389 and then #388 and #390 merged. Slice 1 (#391) remains open as a draft, with one low finding dismissed and a medium tuple-normalization finding handed to a worker along with a merge of main into the branch. Slice 1's own report, Chakra perf check and byte-diff against main were never confirmed.

repo: Caliper work is split into stacked PRs and slices: #388 (Rust 1.99/edition 2024) is the bottom, #390 (tsrs backend) stacks on it, and #391 (slice 1, new PropType variants) follows. Later slices are S2 checker-to-PropType converter, S3 React terminals by declaring path, S4 checker wins behind the structural-first window.

Slice 1 bumps SCHEMA_VERSION to 5 and CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION to 33, and replaces wildcard match arms in serializer, display and TOON with exhaustive matches. Version bumps must stay unique and ordered when main moves them.
PropType::Truncated and TruncationLimit exist in the schema before any producer (intended for S2 per ADR 0026); that is accepted practice, so the low finding was dismissed.

TypeScript normalizes tuples via createNormalizedTupleType: an optional element before a required one becomes required with undefined added. resolve_collected_type did not do this for `[...[string?], number]`.
Likely overlap files with the tsrs backend merge: crates/semantic/src/convert.rs, types/semantic.rs, and the architecture-test allow-list.
Construct-suite goldens come from the Go checker, and new tuple rows go under tuples-arrays/.

code.finding: Expected conflict hotspot when merging main (with tsrs backend) into feat/proptype-variants; line numbers were not given.

workflow: A task-notification saying an agent is waiting on background work is interim and carries no report; check the branch, CI and commit message directly instead of waiting.

When the same bug class shows up twice (tuple splicing without normalization), fix the pattern: enumerate the sites, derive rules from the reference implementation, centralize in one function, and add a table test failing on the tip.
Avoid two processes pushing to one branch; sequence the merge after the fix worker's push.
Prefer a merge commit of main over rebase and force-push when a worker is pushing to the branch.
GitHub's mergeability status can disagree with `git merge-tree`; verify both before assuming a real conflict.
Don't guess at ambiguous names like 'eaves'; search and ask, as it would waste tokens on the wrong repo.

friction: Slice 1 worker ran about 49 minutes and 550k tokens, 306 tool calls, and still delivered no final report.
PR #391 showed CONFLICTING on GitHub while git merge-tree showed a clean merge.
The user mentioned 'eaves' work that matches no project, branch or trail, costing a clarification round; the user replied to ignore it.
Slice 1's diff showed 466 files against #388's base because of merged construct-suite fixtures, which obscured the real size.
Entire Gates approval was the only failing check on #390, so progress depended on user approvals.
